features.name: Academic preparation
features.description: The highest level of formal technical education presented as preparation for the role.

levels.descriptor: Bachelor's degree or equivalent only, with no advanced degree signal.
Master's degree in a relevant technical field.
Doctoral degree in a relevant technical field.

features.name: Agentic systems design
features.description: Experience designing or owning agent-based systems, especially their boundaries, supervision, permissions, and backend control planes.

levels.descriptor: No agent-based tooling experience is shown.
The letter mentions agents or autonomous workflows only in general terms.
The letter describes a recognizable agent architecture, typically pairing Python agents with Go services.
The letter shows deliberate control design for agents, such as permissions, auditability, bounded actions, or explicit end-to-end ownership.

features.name: Algorithmic fluency
features.description: Practical command of data structures and algorithms as demonstrated through concrete engineering improvements.

levels.descriptor: No algorithmic strength is mentioned.
Algorithmic fluency is claimed, but without a concrete example.
At least one specific redesign or optimization shows applied algorithmic thinking.
Multiple or especially vivid examples show data structures and algorithms materially shaping system design.

features.name: Applied AI production maturity
features.description: The depth of real-world AI or LLM experience, especially reliable deployment, evaluation, and operational safeguards.

levels.descriptor: No AI experience is mentioned.
Mentions AI or LLM exposure without concrete deployment detail.
Describes shipped AI features or workflows in production.
Describes shipped AI work plus evaluation, hardening, guardrails, or trustworthiness practices.

features.name: Developer enablement mindset
features.description: Whether the letter frames security engineering as helping developers work safely through usable defaults, lower friction, and internal-user empathy.

levels.descriptor: No developer-centered security philosophy is visible.
Shows generic interest in improving security but not specifically in making life easier for developers.
Explicitly talks about secure-by-default workflows, reducing friction, or helping teams do the right thing.
Strongly frames security as developer enablement, emphasizing defaults, tools, or guardrails over policing, process, or documents.

features.name: Evidence specificity
features.description: How much the letter backs claims with concrete examples, mechanisms, named systems, or technical detail.

levels.descriptor: Relies mostly on generic claims or alignment statements.
Provides some concrete terms or examples but not enough to let the reader picture the work.
Uses several specific examples, mechanisms, or outcomes to support claims.
Is densely grounded in concrete evidence, with enough operational detail that the work feels tangible and credible.

features.name: Go depth
features.description: How central and substantial Go appears in the applicant's production backend experience.

levels.descriptor: No meaningful Go evidence.
Mentions Go, but without clear depth or ownership.
Shows regular production use of Go in recent work.
Makes Go clearly central, such as a principal language or daily driver tied to sustained backend ownership.

features.name: Impact articulation
features.description: How clearly the letter explains the outcomes or practical effects of the applicant's work.

levels.descriptor: Lists tasks with no visible outcomes.
Hints at benefit but remains mostly activity-based.
States clear outcomes such as reduced manual work, faster systems, or fewer bugs.
Shows strong leverage language, tying work to capacity, attention saved, or meaningful organizational effect.

features.name: Narrative coherence
features.description: How well the letter forms a connected story that links background, motivations, and role fit rather than reading like a list.

levels.descriptor: Reads mainly as a list of qualifications with little story connecting them.
Includes some motivation or a loose arc, but the connection from past experience to this role is not especially strong.
Builds a clear through-line from prior experience to interest in this role.
Presents a distinctive, memorable narrative or professional thesis that makes the application feel intentional and well-shaped.

features.name: Narrative voice
features.description: How distinctive, memorable, and non-formulaic the letter's voice or framing feels.

levels.descriptor: Reads as flat, list-like, or heavily templated prose.
Is competent and readable, but largely generic in voice.
Has a noticeable hook, framing device, or coherent personal story.
Has a strong, memorable voice that reinforces fit without sacrificing substance.

features.name: Offensive security practice
features.description: Ongoing attacker-oriented practice outside routine development work, such as CTFs or similar exercises.

levels.descriptor: No offensive-practice evidence is mentioned.
Mentions casual or occasional participation with little detail.
Shows regular participation presented as deliberate skill maintenance.
Shows strong results or serious competitive commitment that signals sustained offensive practice.

features.name: Open-source stewardship
features.description: Responsibility for code, maintenance, or users in public software ecosystems beyond the applicant's employer.

levels.descriptor: No open-source activity is mentioned.
Mentions occasional patches or minor contributions.
Shows regular contributions or maintainership of a small project.
Maintains a project with outside users or community responsibilities such as reviews, releases, issue handling, or roadmap decisions.

features.name: Ownership seniority
features.description: How much direct ownership, autonomy, and delivery responsibility the applicant claims for the work described.

levels.descriptor: Mostly aspirational language or support-role contribution.
Shows some hands-on contribution but limited ownership.
Shows clear ownership of tools, systems, or reviews.
Shows repeated architecture, design, or lead responsibility with independent judgment.

features.name: Personal project ambition
features.description: The technical ambition and substance of self-directed engineering projects outside normal job duties.

levels.descriptor: No personal project is mentioned.
Mentions a small utility or light side project with modest technical scope.
Describes a substantive side project with meaningful systems or infrastructure work.
Describes an ambitious self-directed systems project tackling distributed correctness, recovery, delivery guarantees, or similarly hard engineering problems.

features.name: Platform leverage orientation
features.description: Whether the applicant is motivated by foundational infrastructure or tooling whose benefits compound across many teams or products.

levels.descriptor: Does not show any particular interest in foundational or shared systems work.
Mentions scale or impact in passing, but not as a central motivation.
Explicitly values platform or infrastructure work because it benefits many teams.
Persuasively frames central tooling as a multiplier, emphasizing inherited impact or organization-wide capacity gains.

features.name: Production delivery scope
features.description: The breadth and depth of hands-on responsibility for shipping, maintaining, testing, or operating production systems.

levels.descriptor: Describes launching or owning only a small number of production services, such as 2.
Describes a moderate shipped footprint, such as about 4 production services.
Describes repeated launch and maintenance experience across many services, such as 6 or more.

features.name: Programming language breadth
features.description: The range of additional programming languages the applicant claims beyond the core required stack.

levels.descriptor: No additional languages are mentioned.
Mentions 1 to 2 additional languages.
Mentions 3 to 5 additional languages.
Mentions more than 5 additional languages.

features.name: Python depth
features.description: How substantive the applicant's production Python experience appears for services, tooling, automation, or agents.

levels.descriptor: Python is absent or appears only incidentally.
Python is mentioned as a tool or companion language, but depth is unclear.
The letter shows regular production Python use for tooling, automation, prototypes, or services.
Python is portrayed as a major production language with broad, concrete use across services, automation, and agent behavior.

features.name: Relevant professional tenure
features.description: The amount of directly relevant professional software-engineering experience the letter claims.

levels.descriptor: Below the role minimum or unclear on relevant experience length.
Roughly meets the minimum, around 2 to 3 years of relevant experience.
Shows solid mid-level experience, around 4 to 5 years.
Shows strong experience depth, around 6 or more years.

features.name: Reliability / maintainer mindset
features.description: Whether the letter emphasizes maintainability, failure-awareness, operability, and long-term care for systems.

levels.descriptor: Shows no explicit maintainability or reliability orientation.
Implies care for quality but not as a recurring theme.
Clearly values maintainable, dependable systems or draws on maintenance experience.
Makes long-term operability a central lens, emphasizing inheritance, quiet resilience, or higher standards for security-critical software.

features.name: Role-specific fit
features.description: How specifically and convincingly the letter explains motivation and alignment for this exact role or team and maps the applicant's background to its responsibilities.

levels.descriptor: Motivation is generic and mostly repeats the company, title, or desire to apply.
The letter links interest to security or scale, but the reason remains broad.
The letter gives clear role-specific motivation tied to security automation, vulnerability handling, or the team's mandate.
The letter opens with a memorable thesis about the problem space and repeatedly connects that thesis to the applicant's background.

features.name: Security assessment practice
features.description: The depth of hands-on experience assessing systems or code for security issues and following findings through remediation.

levels.descriptor: Does not mention security assessment work.
Refers to reviews or security thinking vaguely without concrete methods.
Describes performing assessments such as threat modeling, code review, or attack-surface analysis.
Shows structured assessment practice with clear methods and follow-through such as remediation validation or recurring ownership.

features.name: Security automation framing
features.description: How well the letter understands the role as scaling security work through automation, tooling, and systems design rather than manual process.

levels.descriptor: Does not clearly articulate security automation as a central problem of the role.
Mentions reducing manual toil or automating repetitive work in general terms.
Clearly frames the role as scaling response capacity, expert attention, or organization-wide security effort.
Shows nuanced systems thinking about automation, such as variant analysis, triage strategy, scarce-expert amplification, or vulnerability response as a design problem.

features.name: Security certifications
features.description: The strength of formal external security credentials cited as validation of security knowledge or hands-on skill.

levels.descriptor: No relevant security certification is stated.
A baseline or survey credential such as Security+ is stated.
A rigorous hands-on credential such as OSCP or a similarly demanding practical certification is stated.

features.name: Security engineering mindset/rigor
features.description: Whether the letter conveys mature security-oriented thinking and an unusually high standard of rigor for security-sensitive engineering.

levels.descriptor: Gives no clear signal of a personal engineering ethic around security-critical systems.
Implies care or correctness, but only indirectly.
States a clear philosophy of rigor, resilience, or seriousness about security work.
Conveys a distinctive and convincing personal ethic about holding security-sensitive systems to a higher standard.

features.name: Vulnerability triage automation
features.description: Direct experience building tooling that automates vulnerability intake, triage, routing, deduplication, prioritization, or similar workflows.

levels.descriptor: The letter does not describe vulnerability-handling automation.
The letter mentions security automation in general, but not a specific vulnerability triage workflow.
The letter shows direct experience automating intake, classification, routing, or deduplication of vulnerability reports.
The letter shows a clear transformation of a manual vulnerability workflow or explicitly states operational impact from the automation.

features.name: Writing polish
features.description: The degree of proofreading, grammatical correctness, and surface-level professionalism in the prose.

levels.descriptor: Frequent errors repeatedly interrupt reading or seriously undermine credibility.
Noticeable proofreading problems distract the reader more than once.
Contains some typos, but the letter remains easy to follow.
Mostly clean, with at most a minor slip.
Polished and effectively error-free at a professional standard.

other.name: Other
other.description: Dimensions that do not clearly belong to any broader recurring construct.

levels.descriptor: No collaboration signal appears beyond applying for the role.
Cross-functional work is implied, but the posture toward security specialists is not explicit.
The letter explicitly shows enthusiasm for close collaboration with security engineers or learning from specialist teammates.
